questions.stem: Which Indian state has the longest total coastline among all states?

options.option_text: Gujarat (approx. 1,600 km, India's longest state coastline)
Tamil Nadu (approx. 1,076 km along the Coromandel Coast)
Andhra Pradesh (approx. 974 km along the Bay of Bengal)
Maharashtra (approx. 720 km along the Konkan coastline)

questions.explanation: Gujarat, with its irregular peninsular shape and the Gulf of Kutch, has a coastline of approximately 1,600 km — the longest of any Indian state. Tamil Nadu (second-longest at ~1,076 km) is the most common wrong answer because it borders two seas, but its coastline is still significantly shorter than Gujarat's.

questions.stem: Which is the smallest Indian state in terms of geographical area?

options.option_text: Sikkim (7,096 sq km, fifth-smallest, borders Nepal and Tibet)
Tripura (10,486 sq km, three sides bordered by Bangladesh)
Goa (3,702 sq km, former Portuguese colony on west coast)
Manipur (22,327 sq km, shares border with Myanmar in east)

questions.explanation: Goa, at approximately 3,702 sq km, is the smallest Indian state by area. Sikkim is the second-smallest and is the most tempting distractor because it is perceived as remote and tiny, but it is nearly twice the area of Goa. Note: Lakshadweep UT is smaller still, but it is not a state.

questions.stem: The 'Cheraw', a traditional dance performed with rhythmically clapped bamboo poles, is officially recognised as the state folk dance of which Indian state?

options.option_text: Manipur (famous for classical Manipuri style and Thang-ta traditions)
Nagaland (known for War Dances and Hornbill Festival tribal performances)
Meghalaya (home to the Nongkrem Dance of the Khasi hill community)
Mizoram (Cheraw performed by the Mizo community at festivals)

questions.explanation: Cheraw (Bamboo Dance) originates from the Mizo people of Mizoram and is recognised as the state's representative folk dance. It is frequently highlighted in national cultural programmes. Nagaland is the most tempting wrong answer because bamboo is also prominent in its tribal culture, but its signature event is the Hornbill Festival, not Cheraw.

questions.stem: Which Indian state produces the dominant share of the country's black pepper output, earning it recognition as the 'Land of Spices'?

options.option_text: Karnataka (Coorg region is a leading coffee and secondary pepper producer)
Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris hills are known for cardamom, tea, and coffee)
Andhra Pradesh (Guntur district is India's largest chilli-producing region)
Kerala (accounts for over 95% of India's total black pepper production)

questions.explanation: Kerala, particularly districts like Wayanad and Idukki, produces over 95% of India's black pepper. Karnataka is the most tempting distractor because Coorg/Kodagu is known for pepper cultivation, but its share is a distant second. The 'Spices Board of India' is also headquartered in Kochi, Kerala.

questions.stem: Namdapha National Park, one of the world's only protected areas known to shelter all four large wild cat species found in India, is located in which state?

options.option_text: Assam (Kaziranga is famous for one-horned rhino, not all four large cats)
Nagaland (Intanki National Park is the sole national park in this state)
Arunachal Pradesh (Namdapha in Changlang district, easternmost India)
Manipur (Keibul Lamjao is the world's only floating national park)

questions.explanation: Namdapha National Park in Changlang district, Arunachal Pradesh, shelters the Bengal tiger, Indian leopard, snow leopard, and clouded leopard — a combination found in virtually no other park globally. Assam is the most common wrong answer due to its many famous wildlife reserves, but none hosts all four large cat species simultaneously.

questions.stem: After the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966 bifurcated the then-Punjab into two states, Chandigarh was retained as a Union Territory. It currently serves as the joint capital of which pair of states?

options.option_text: Punjab and Himachal Pradesh (Shimla was retained as Himachal's own capital)
Punjab and Haryana (Chandigarh became the shared capital after 1966 bifurcation)
Haryana and Himachal Pradesh (no common administrative or capital linkage)
Punjab and Rajasthan (geographically separated with no shared-capital history)

questions.explanation: The 1966 Act split undivided Punjab into Punjab (Punjabi-speaking) and Haryana (Hindi-speaking). Chandigarh, being a planned city on the border, was made a Union Territory and designated as the capital for both new states pending a final allocation that has never occurred. Punjab and Himachal Pradesh is the most tempting wrong answer because Himachal was also carved out of Punjab, but Himachal retains Shimla as its own capital.

questions.stem: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution creates Autonomous District Councils to safeguard tribal customary law and traditions. Which of the following states is NOT covered under the Sixth Schedule?

options.option_text: Assam (Bodoland Territorial Council operates under the Sixth Schedule)
Tripura (Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council under Sixth Schedule)
Nagaland (governed under Article 371-A special provisions, not Sixth Schedule)
Mizoram (Chakma and Lai Autonomous District Councils function under Sixth Schedule)

questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule applies to Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. Nagaland is explicitly excluded because its unique tribal governance is instead protected under Article 371-A, which shields Naga customary law and land rights from ordinary parliamentary legislation. Mizoram is the most tempting wrong answer since it shares a cultural belt with Nagaland, but Mizoram's Mizo National Front–era peace accord was implemented through the Sixth Schedule framework, not 371-A.
